name: STAGE ROAD & COACH STOP
materialIdentity: cold indigo, grey and sky, with warm ochre and gold only where the lamp and the windows reach -- ruling 17a. The only night exterior in the game.
note: Doc 05 Room 1 plus doc 17 v2, with errata ruling 19a's canonical per-state line sets. Doc 17 note 3: THE ROAD EAST's LISTEN variants 2 and 3 are identical to each other AND to the line at the high ridge in Act IV -- three uses of 'Nothing coming', a hundred yards and fifteen hours apart. Do not vary them. THE COACH, THE TEAM and THE WATCHMAN'S LAMP are state-gated: the coach becomes THE ROAD WEST OUT once it has gone, the team exists only while it is here, and there is no lamp at all until Hob walks onto the road.

cycling.note: Doc 18: a carried flame in still air, not a torch. It is the brightest and only warm object in the frame and must not draw more attention than a lamp deserves. Four entries at the top of accent_gold, reserved -- which is also what now keeps the coach lantern and the clasp on Thad's case below it, a rule doc 17 stated and nothing was checking.

Doc 18: moonlight on standing water shifting as air moves over it, barely perceptible. The phase offset is per puddle and costs no extra entries -- each streak is painted with a different one of the three reserved indices, so the same rotation shows each of them a different part of the cycle. That is how the technique did it in 1990.

LOOK_AT.say: Everything I own, and a tuning fork. The tuning fork is the valuable part.
repeat: Everything I own. It is not heavy and that is the whole difficulty.
My father packed it. He put the fork in first, which tells you what he thought of the rest.

LISTEN_TO.say: The fork, faintly, against the clasp. A. Four hundred and forty. It is the only correct thing within a hundred miles.
repeat: The fork against the clasp. A. It is still four hundred and forty.
Nothing. I have stopped shaking it to hear it, which is a low thing to be caught doing.

overrides.OPEN: A shirt, a razor, three letters, and a tuning fork. I have checked it four times since Sacramento and the contents have been consistent.
overrides.PICK_UP: I have it. I have had it the entire time.

LOOK_AT.say: A lamp, crossing the road. There is a man behind it and he has not looked at me.
repeat: Still crossing. He is in no hurry and he is not lost.
The only lit thing on this road, and it is going the other way.

LISTEN_TO.say: Footsteps. Even ones. He is counting them.
repeat: Still even.
He has not broken stride once. Not once, in the whole length of the road.

overrides.TALK_TO: He is walking. I shall let him walk.

LOOK_AT.say: The lamp, away up the street. It has not once looked back at me.
repeat: Small now.
Gone round the corner and taken the only light with it.

LISTEN_TO.say: Nothing. He has taken the sound with him too.
repeat: Nothing.
Nothing at all.

LOOK_AT.say: A stage coach, halted, with my case coming down off the back. It has come four hundred miles and it looks it.
repeat: The near wheel has been repaired twice with two different woods.
There is a great deal of dust on it and none of it is from here.

LISTEN_TO.say: The team, shifting. The near axle is dry — it has been dry a long time.
repeat: Still dry. It will be heard from.
Somebody up top is rearranging the load and swearing about it.

overrides.USE: It is going. It is going with some enthusiasm.
overrides.PULL: I have considered running after it. I would like that on the record and nowhere else.

LOOK_AT.say: Two horses I can see and I am told there are four more. They have their heads down and they have earned it.
repeat: Nobody has unhitched them. We are not stopping long.
The near one has looked at me twice, which is twice more than the driver.

LISTEN_TO.say: Breathing, and harness. It is the most contented sound on this road.
repeat: Shifting. One of them is bored.
Nothing. They have gone to sleep standing up, which I did not know was available.

LOOK_AT.say: Gone. It made very good time on the way out.
repeat: Not another one for four days. I have checked twice and the answer did not improve.
The ruts are still filling in. That is the whole of my connection to the rest of the world, filling in.

LISTEN_TO.say: The near axle, going away. It will fail on somebody else's stretch.
repeat: Faint now.
Nothing. It is a long way off.

LOOK_AT.say: CONSOLATION — POP. 2,000 AND CLIMBING. The 'and climbing' is in a different hand, and was added later.
repeat: The number has been repainted four times. You can see the smaller ones underneath, each of them once true.
The smallest number underneath is two hundred. Somebody was pleased with two hundred once.

LISTEN_TO.say: It creaks. It would like to be taken down.
repeat: Creaking. It would still like to be taken down.
Nothing. The wind has dropped and it has stopped complaining.

overrides.PULL: It is nailed to a post, in the ground, at the edge of a town. I have been here two minutes and I am already vandalising the place.

LOOK_AT.say: Home is that way. It is eleven hundred miles that way, which robs the gesture of some of its force.
repeat: Eleven hundred miles. I have just come along it and it did not feel optional at the time.
Home is that way. I am not going to keep looking at it.
Nothing coming.
Nothing coming.

overrides.USE: That would be a decision, and I have only just made one.

LOOK_AT.say: Mud. I have been assured it improves.
repeat: It has come over the top of my boots, which I had not thought possible in the first minute.
Mud. I have been in this territory for ninety seconds and I have formed a view.

LISTEN_TO.say: Nothing. Mud is the only honest thing in the territory and it has nothing to say.
repeat: Nothing. It is entirely uninterested.
Nothing. I am going to stop asking it things.

overrides.PICK_UP: I have enough on my boots. I am carrying a quantity of this town already.

LOOK_AT.say: Consolation. There are lamps on in about a third of it.
repeat: Somebody is still awake down there, and somebody is playing a piano badly, and those are two separate facts.
Two hundred yards. It is the shortest part of the journey and I am putting it off.

LISTEN_TO.say: A town, at night, half of it asleep. A piano, flat, some distance off.
repeat: Still flat. Whoever is playing it is not the problem.
Somebody laughing. It is the first cheerful sound I have heard since Sacramento.
